'''Raymond (Ray) John Heaphy Beverton''' [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | last1 = Cushing | first1 = D. H. | authorlink1 = David Cushing| last2 = Edwards | first2 = R. W. | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.1996.0003  | doi-access = free| title = Raymond John Heaphy Beverton, C. B. E. 29 August 1922 – 23 July 1995 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 42 | pages = 24–38 | year = 1996 }}</ref> (29 August 1922 – 23 July 1995) was an important founder of [[fisheries science]]. He is best known for the book ''On the Dynamics of Exploited Fish Populations''<ref name="B-H">Beverton, R. J. H., and Holt, S. J. 1957. On the Dynamics of Exploited Fish Populations. Fishery Investigations Series II. Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food, London. 533 pp.</ref> (1957) which he wrote with [[Sidney Holt]]. The book is a cornerstone of modern fisheries science and remains much used today. Beverton's life and achievements are described in detail in several obituaries written by prominent figures in fisheries science.<ref name="frs"/><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Cushing | first1 = D. | title = Ray Beverton, 1922–1995: A personal tribute | doi = 10.1111/j.1095-8649.1995.tb06018.x | journal = Journal of Fish Biology | volume = 47 | issue = 6 | pages = 929–930 | year = 1995 | bibcode = 1995JFBio..47..929C }}</ref><ref>[http://www2.fisheries.com/files/Misc.%20Publications.pdf] Pauly, D. 1996. Some reflections on Professor Ray Beverton, FRS, 1922–1995. ICES/CIEM Information, 27: 16.</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Pitcher | first1 = T. J. | title = Obituary: Raymond John Heaphy Beverton, CBE, FRS | doi = 10.1139/f96-145 | journal = Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences | volume = 53 | issue = 5 | pages = 1200–1201 | year = 1996 | bibcode = 1996CJFAS..53.1200P }}</ref><ref name="Ramster">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1006/jmsc.1996.0001 | last = Ramster| first = John| title = Professor Ray Beverton 29 August 1922 – 23 July 1995 | journal = ICES Journal of Marine Science | volume = 53 | pages = 1–9| year = 1996 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Shelton | first1 = R. G. J. | last2 = Hawkins | first2 = A. D. | last3 = Holt | first3 = S. | doi = 10.1007/BF01103812 | title = Professor Raymond (John Heaphy) Beverton, CBE, FRS, FIBiol | journal = Reviews in Fish Biology and Fisheries | volume = 5 | issue = 4 | pages = 393 | year = 1995 | s2cid = 27631037 | doi-access = free | bibcode = 1995RFBF....5..393S }}</ref>

==Achievements==
Much of the foundations of quantitative fisheries science were laid out in ''On the Dynamics of Exploited Fish Populations''<ref name="B-H" /> which Ray Beverton and [[Sidney Holt]] wrote at the Fisheries Laboratory, Lowestoft (UK). In his review of the 1993 reprint of the book, [[Ray Hilborn]] writes "It is remarkable how the book has stood the test of time and still provides a survey of the important topics in fisheries management".<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1007/BF00044132 | last = Hilborn| first = Ray| authorlink = Ray Hilborn| title = Book Reviews: ''On the Dynamics of Exploited Fish Populations'' | journal = Reviews in Fish Biology and Fisheries | volume = 4 | issue = 2 | pages = 259–260 | year = 1994 | s2cid = 29055031}}</ref> The book has a new reprint from 2004, with a foreword by Sidney Holt.

Beverton was also one of the first to acknowledge the variation of life histories that exists in fish, and the importance of this in [[fisheries management]]. This was the topic of the symposium ''Building on Beverton's legacy: Life history variation and fisheries management'',<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Shuter | first1 = B. J. | last2 = Abrams | first2 = P. A. | doi = 10.1139/F05-067 | title = Introducing the symposium "Building on Beverton's legacy: Life history variation and fisheries management" | journal = Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences | volume = 62 | issue = 4 | pages = 725 | year = 2005 | bibcode = 2005CJFAS..62..725S }}</ref> organised in 2003 during the 133rd annual meeting of the [[American Fisheries Society]]. The legacy of the 1957 Beverton and Holt treatise is commemorated in the volume ''Advances in Fisheries Science. 50 years on from Beverton and Holt''.<ref>{{Cite book | editor1-last = Payne | editor1-first = Andy | editor2-first = John | editor3-first = Ted | doi = 10.1002/9781444302653 | title = Advances in Fisheries Science | year = 2008 | isbn = 9781444302653 | editor2-last = Cotter | editor3-last = Potter | doi-access = free }}</ref> The volume includes a foreword by [[Sidney Holt]].

Beverton was the editor of ''Journal du Conseil'', now ''ICES Journal of Marine Science'', from 1983 to 1991. Among many other posts, he was the Deputy Director of the Fisheries Laboratory, Lowestoft.<ref name="Ramster" /> Beverton stayed active until his late years; he was involved in several papers published after his death, the last one nine years afterwards.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Beverton | first1 = R. J. H. | last2 = Hylen | first2 = A. | last3 = Østvedt | first3 = O. -J. | last4 = Alvsvaag | first4 = J. | last5 = Iles | first5 = T. C. | title = Growth, maturation, and longevity of maturation cohorts of Norwegian spring-spawning herring | doi = 10.1016/j.icesjms.2004.01.001 | journal = ICES Journal of Marine Science | volume = 61 | issue = 2 | pages = 165 | year = 2004 | doi-access = free | bibcode = 2004ICJMS..61..165B }}</ref> Outside fisheries science, Beverton is best known for the [[Beverton–Holt model]]. In [[population ecology]] the model is used as a stand-alone discrete time population model or as a model of density dependence in larger population models. Originally the model had a more specific usage; it was devised to describe the dependence of recruitment on spawning stock biomass.

===Beverton Medal===

The [[Fisheries Society of the British Isles]] awards each year the [[Beverton Medal]] "to a distinguished scientist for a lifelong contribution to all aspects of the study of fish biology and/or fisheries science, with a focus on ground-breaking research."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fsbi.org.uk/information/medals/ |title=The medals |author=The Fisheries Society of the British Isles}}</ref> The history of the medal goes back to 1995 when the society decided to award a medal to an individual who had contributed significantly to fisheries biology. Ray Beverton was the first recipient, but he died soon afterwards. The medal was then named in his honour.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fsbi.org.uk/information/history/ |title=The history of the society |author=The Fisheries Society of the British Isles}}</ref>
